title: Supervised run continuation blocked: journal stranded at START_CLAUDE (crash window with no CLI driver) and both operator recovery paths denied by the session permission classifier
affects: M2-T015 (supervised-auto product proof #1: unit 1 deliverables complete, committed cabe128 on task/M2-T015-survey-ingestion; units 2+ cannot dispatch until the supervised runtime is recoverable)
detail: SUPERVISED-AUTO activation itself succeeded and is fully evidenced (D-010 source-023; PR #189; project-control/reports/ACTIVATION-2026-08-08-supervised-auto/). During M2-T015, after the operator's legal clear-recovery, a re-dispatched start was externally killed between the preflight_pass->START_CLAUDE journal commit and the worker launch (Job Object took the child down; zero orphans; zero pending external effects; audit chain verifies). The journal is stranded at START_CLAUDE: the S7 table's only exits (claude_start_failed->HALTED, then HALTED->IDLE via owner_explicit_restart) have NO CLI or production driver for this window; recover_boot classifies SAFE_CHECKPOINT but records only; start correctly refuses with bad_cycle_entry_state. This is an AD-093-qualifying unresolved crash/recovery gap (supervisor-freeze rule section 2) registered for a future defect-lane task - NOT fixed inside M2-T015 (D-010-R216/R229). The orchestrator attempted two recovery paths and the session permission classifier denied both: (1) firing the two S7-legal, factually-true transitions through the supervisor's own StateMachine/AuditLog API from the checkout; (2) continuing on a fresh --runtime-base (existing CLI input; R595-leg precedent) with the stranded runtime preserved untouched as defect evidence. Per the denial guidance and D-008, the orchestrator stopped and returned the choice to the owner instead of working around the classifier.
